# Use an optional remote capability safely

Use when a goal needs Git history, GitHub, Jira, or another consequential provider operation. Local work remains the default and must continue when the provider is unavailable.

## Procedure

1. Run `tasktra capabilities --root <root>` and `tasktra status --root <root> --goal-id <goal>`. A Codex or connector host may supply a credential-free, one-invocation snapshot with `--provider-health <report.json>`; this reports capability only and grants no authority. Do not probe credentials or treat provider loss as a local-work blocker.
2. For reads, use only a registered read-only descriptor with the exact resource scope. Bound results and retain concise evidence references instead of copying full provider payloads.
3. Before a write, verify an active version-2 authority envelope, the exact allowed action and effect class, an exact contained provider resource scope, a current approval for a distinct performer, an active work lease, and a stable idempotency key. Keep the closed descriptor and request in short JSON files without credentials.
4. Prepare locally with `tasktra effect --root <root> provider-prepare <key> --goal-id <goal> --work-unit-id <unit> --descriptor <descriptor.json> --request <request.json> --work-attempt-id <attempt> --envelope-sha256 <sha256> --actor <performer>`. Supply the lease through `TASKTRA_LEASE_TOKEN` or the selected `--lease-token-env`; never print or persist it.
5. Invoke the effect only through a configured host integration that constructs the closed provider registry and calls `ProviderEffectExecutor.execute`. The executor atomically acquires the dispatch slot, invokes the registered adapter with the persisted request, and records the sanitized receipt. `tasktra effect --root <root> provider-execute <key> --descriptor <descriptor.json> --actor <performer>` is the built-in executor entry point for a configured GitHub CLI adapter; it cannot execute an unprepared or differently described effect. Never place a manual provider call between ledger CLI commands. If no executor-backed adapter is configured, leave the effect pending and report the provider unavailable.
6. Reconcile an indeterminate outcome only through `ProviderEffectExecutor.reconcile`, whose registered adapter performs the exact read. Manual `provider-reconcile` is recovery-only and may record `applied` or `conflict`, never absence. Only an adapter-proven absence bound to the committed reconciliation event can make a retry eligible; GitHub non-idempotent writes deliberately never claim retry-safe absence.
7. Run `tasktra audit --root <root> verify` and report the intent key, effect-attempt ID, sanitized receipt or reconciliation, capability degradation, and next safe action.

Credentials belong only to the host or connected provider. Never place tokens, authorization headers, credential-bearing URLs, lease tokens, or raw provider errors in project files, prompts, audit data, handoffs, or receipts. Git pushes additionally require exact expected-old and new object IDs; conflicts stop rather than overwrite.
